description: The application reads the cache, loads from the database on a miss and stores the result. Writes go to the database and invalidate the key.
Time to live: how long an entry stays fresh. It bounds staleness even when an invalidation is missed.
Many requests miss the same key at once and all hit the database. Fixed with in-flight deduplication, locks or early refresh.
Removing an entry after the source changes. The hard part is ordering it correctly with concurrent reads.
Caching "not found" (`null`) too, so repeated lookups for missing ids do not reach the database.
Serve the expired value immediately and refresh it in the background; the same idea as the HTTP header and SWR on the frontend.
